requirements.text: On a split button where the sheen is in use (`focusSheen` on or `sheenTrigger` supplied), the chevron's existing one-time mount streak does not play, so two streaks never overlap; on split buttons without the sheen the mount streak is unchanged.

A host plays the streak from code with an optional `sheenTrigger` value (a string or a number): every change of the value plays one sweep on a button that need not be focused, while the first value on mount plays nothing; it works whether or not `focusSheen` is on.
The programmatic trigger also works on a split control (one sweep across the whole control) and on disabled and busy buttons, while the focus trigger never applies to disabled buttons.
When the user's system asks for reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`), neither the focus streak nor the programmatic trigger shows a sweep, and there is no override.

Private hook that turns a changing trigger value into one replayable sweep. The button needs a tiny piece of state to remember the value it mounted with and to notice each later change without a ref handle or a timer.

Restart a finished pseudo-element animation by alternating keyframe names. A sweep must genuinely replay on every trigger change, including after the previous sweep ended, without remounting the button or forcing a reflow.

Document the programmatic streak everywhere the feature is documented. The new option is only usable if people reading the library pages can find what it does, how it differs from focusSheen and how reduced motion affects it.

R6: a split button given a sheenTrigger suppresses the chevron mount streak
R6: regular buttons have no mount streak and gain no extra chevron layer
R6: a split button mounted and then immediately focused shows only the whole-control layer

R6: suppressing the mount streak leaves no empty layout layer
R6: a split button that does not use the sheen keeps its one-time chevron mount streak
R6: a regular button has no chevron mount streak to suppress and gains no sheen class

tests: R8: a split control sweeps once across the whole control per trigger change

R8: a busy button plays a sweep and keeps its aria-busy and spinner state
R8: a disabled button never shows a focus streak
R8: a button that is both disabled and busy plays exactly one sweep per change
R8: the sweep is not restarted when the busy state ends part-way
R8: the band is visible on the disabled colours of every style

tests: R9: reduced motion removes both bands entirely, with no override

R9: reduced motion leaves the focus ring and other feedback alone
A3: the pages say reduced motion disables both triggers and that no prop overrides it
